item.description:
PDF highlights cover every page they span, footnotes write themselves out in the margin, Scribe has Go and Reader menus, the command palette finds your pieces again, and large libraries use less memory.

  • Fixed: highlighting a passage that runs onto the next page of a PDF only marked the first page. The highlight now covers every page it spans, stays one highlight with one note, and is removed in full when you delete it.
  • Jumping to a PDF highlight now brings the start of the highlight into view, not the text just below it.
  • Fixed: if permanently deleting an item from the bin failed part-way, the library could keep an entry whose files were gone. Scribe now finishes or undoes an interrupted deletion the next time it opens.
  • Covers are kept in memory within a fixed budget, so browsing a large library for a long time no longer keeps growing Scribe's memory use.
  • Publishers' cover images are loaded at the size they're shown, in the background, rather than at full size.
  • The cover cache on disk is trimmed as it grows during a session, not only when Scribe opens.
  • Footnotes in the margin now write out one word at a time, in reading order, instead of a line at once.
  • A faint line joins each footnote's number in the text to its note in the margin.
  • Pointing at a footnote number or its note lights up the other, along with the sentence the number belongs to.
  • Footnote numbers and margin notes can be reached with Tab; Return on a note takes you back to its number.
  • New Go menu: Today, Categories, Catalogue and Highlights (⌘1–⌘4), Back (⌘[) and the command palette (⌘K).
  • New Reader menu for the open piece: Info, Reading Format, text size, previous and next chapter in books, the stack, favourites, Open Original and Close Reader.
  • File ▸ Save… (⌘N) and Edit ▸ Search Catalogue / Find in Page (⌘F) are in the menu bar too, and work while reading.
  • Fixed: searching in the command palette (⌘K) listed commands under the names of other rows instead of the pieces that matched.
  • The palette's search field is ready to type into as soon as it opens.

Give any piece a subtitle, find categories in alphabetical order, and books and PDFs follow "Open where I left off".

  • Fixed: deleting pieces you'd recently highlighted could leave Today's Marginalia empty, even with older highlights elsewhere.
  • Fixed: with "Open where I left off" turned off, books still opened at the chapter you were last reading.
  • Fixed: with it off, a PDF's page indicator and progress briefly showed your old page while the first page was on screen.
  • Categories now appear in alphabetical order on the Departments page, in Settings and in every category picker, so they're quicker to find and stay put when you add or rename one.
  • Category pickers in the Info panel and the import sheet list subcategories under their department, as the right-click menu already did.
  • The Info panel has a subtitle under the title. Add or edit one for any article, book or PDF, or clear it to remove it. An empty subtitle shows nowhere else.
  • A book's subtitle sits under its title on the opening page, in place of its first chapter's title.

Highlighting and notes work again, with a handful of smaller fixes around Today and the shelves.

  • Fixed: selecting text in an essay, article or book no longer failed to show the highlight and note controls.
  • Fixed: a highlight or note ending on the last character of an article, essay or chapter was saved but never shown.
  • The footer at the bottom of Today shows the version beside “Scribe”, for example “Scribe 2.7.4”.
  • The panel with a piece's details, opened with “i” or ⌘I, is now called Info instead of Colophon.
  • Fixed: hovering over a book on a category's shelf showed a title tip that could be cut off at the top or at either end of the shelf.
  • On a wide window, the three cards in From the backlog now sit together in the middle of the table instead of spreading out to its edges.
